tips.title: Scribing Panel Lines with RB Productions Tools
tips.text: For deep, crisp panel lines, use RB Productions scribing tools. First, lightly sand the surface with 2400 grit sandpaper. Then, using the tool's adjustable depth stop, scribe lines along panel edges. Start with the smallest tool, gradually increasing size to create depth. For complex shapes, use RB Productions curve scribing tool. Apply minimal pressure to avoid damaging details.

tips.title: Photo-Etch Bending with Eduard's PE Bending Jigs
tips.text: Eduard's PE Bending Jigs allow precise bending of photo-etch parts. Insert the part into the jig, then gently bend it over the edge. Use the jig's depth marks for desired angle. For complex bends, use the 90° jig first, then use the 45° jig to fine-tune. Always bend parts before painting, and support them with soft clay or tissue to prevent creases.

tips.title: Airbrush Needle Cleaning with Iwata Brush Cleaner
tips.text: Clean your Iwata airbrush needle regularly to maintain performance. Soak the needle in Iwata Brush Cleaner for 10 minutes, then scrub gently with an Iwata needle brush. Rinse with water and dry with compressed air. For stubborn residue, soak in a solution of warm water and mild detergent, then scrub and rinse. Never use harsh chemicals like acetone.

tips.title: Masking with Tamiya and Kabuki Tapes
tips.text: For precision masking, use Tamiya tape for sharp corners and Kabuki tape for curves. Apply Tamiya tape with a light touch, pressing down from the middle towards the edges. For Kabuki tape, press down firmly for a tight seal, especially around curves. Overlap tapes slightly to prevent paint bleeding. Remove tapes immediately after painting to avoid adhesive residue.

tips.title: Sanding Stick Progression for Smooth Surfaces
tips.text: Achieve smooth surfaces with a progression of sanding sticks. Start with a coarse grit to remove major imperfections, then progress through medium and fine grits. Always sand in the same direction as panel lines. For intricate areas, use dental tools or flexible sanding sticks. Wipe off dust after each grit to avoid scratches.
